processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Alloy ingots with nominal composition Fe-35Mn-17Al-5Cu (at.%) were produced by melting high-purity (>99.9 %) raw materials in a vacuum induction furnace under an argon atmosphere.
Ingots were homogenized at 1200 °C for 24 h.
Homogenized ingots were hot-rolled into plates with a thickness of 4 mm.
Plates were cut into 10 × 5 × 2 mm³ samples by electrical discharge machining for Vickers hardness measurements and microstructure characterizations.
Samples were solution treated at 1100 °C for 10 min under an argon atmosphere, followed by oil quenching (this is the parent process proc_st-1100c-10min-oq).
The solution-treated 17Al sample was aged at 600 °C for 1 h, followed by water quenching. This is the terminal state defining this sample (17Al 600 °C aging 1 h).

structures.overall_structure: After aging at 600 °C for 1 h, the α matrix of the 17Al alloy had almost completely transformed into β-Mn; numerous fine precipitates were distributed within the β-Mn. β-Mn is the dominant (matrix) phase with residual α and fine new precipitates.

interfaces.phase_evolution: α → α + FCC Cu-rich phase → α-Mn + β-Mn + BCC phase → β-Mn + BCC phase + FCC Cu-rich phase (general aging sequence of the Fe-Mn-Al-Cu low-density steels). For the 17Al alloy at 600 °C, the α→β-Mn transformation was almost complete after 1 h.
interfaces.interface_notes: The fine precipitates distributed within the β-Mn of the transformed 17Al alloy were identified as BCC and FCC phases. Detailed TEM interface characterization (β-Mn / FCC Cu-rich with FCC twins) in this paper was performed on the 15Al 600 °C/6 h and 17Al 575 °C/6 h samples, not on the 600 °C/1 h sample.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Vickers microhardness measured with an HVS-1000 digital microhardness tester, load 9.8 N for 15 s; each sample tested 5 times and the average reported.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Load 9.8 N for 15 s; each sample tested 5 times, average of 5 measurements
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure Vickers hardness of the 17Al alloy after aging at 600 °C for 1 h
characterization_methods.key_findings: 17Al alloy aged at 600 °C for 1 h shows a Vickers hardness of 862.7 ± 28.0 HV (Table 3), a large increase over the solution-treated baseline (259.8 ± 1.5 HV).

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: ZEISS Sigma 300 SEM operated at 5 kV
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Polished samples; main panels with 50 µm scale bars and higher-magnification insets
characterization_methods.purpose: Observe the precipitation of secondary phases (α-Mn and β-Mn) after aging
characterization_methods.key_findings: In the 17Al alloy aged at 600 °C for 1 h the matrix is labelled β-Mn and an inset shows numerous fine 'New precipitates'; consistent with near-complete α→β-Mn transformation after 1 h at ≥600 °C.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: GeminiSEM 300 SEM; scanning step size 1.5 μm for low magnification and 0.05 μm for high magnification
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Electrolytically polished samples (10 % perchloric acid + 90 % ethanol)
characterization_methods.purpose: Identify constituent phases and phase evolution after aging treatments
characterization_methods.key_findings: EBSD of the 17Al alloy was performed at 525 °C/10 h, 575 °C/6 h and 650 °C/10 h (not at 600 °C/1 h); it revealed progressive α→β-Mn transformation and new BCC/FCC precipitates within β-Mn.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: 17Al alloy aged at 575 °C for 1 h (selected together with 15Al 550 °C/1 h and 19Al 550 °C/6 h)
characterization_methods.purpose: Identify phase compositions of the alloys
characterization_methods.key_findings: The 17Al XRD pattern (575 °C × 1 h) contained both α-Mn and β-Mn peaks, indicating α-Mn and β-Mn co-precipitated during aging before full α→β-Mn transformation. This XRD test was not performed on the 600 °C/1 h condition.

unmapped_findings: The 17Al alloy chemical composition (EDS, Table 1) is Fe 43.2, Mn 34.8, Al 17.0, Cu 5.0 (at.%).
The density of the 17Al alloy measured by the Archimedes method is 6.76 g/cm³.
The solution-treated (parent state) baseline Vickers hardness of the 17Al alloy is 259.8 ± 1.5 HV.
For the 17Al alloy the α→β-Mn transformation was completed after 6 h at 550 °C, but only after 1 h at 600 °C and above.

Increasing Al content slowed the precipitation kinetics of β-Mn and decreased the fracture toughness of the ultra-hard alloys; the intrinsic hardness of β-Mn was slightly enhanced by higher Al (solid-solution strengthening).
The elastic modulus of the 17Al alloy measured through compressive stress-strain curves was 175 GPa.
